answer:
Fitted the approved ordinal regression (proportional-odds, cumulative-logit/logit link, statsmodels OrderedModel, MLE) on the case-only sample of 148 subjects who developed a COVID-19 AE with a non-missing AESEV (207 AE rows / 189 subjects; 41 excluded for no non-null AESEV). Severity = max AESEV per subject, levels 1<Mild<2<Moderate<3<Severe<4<Life-threatening (distribution 52/82/8/6; BCG 76 vs Placebo 72). Predictors: BCG, MH_count (affirmative MHTERM rows with MHORRES==2, mean 1.38, 0–5), interact_freq (patients_seen midpoints 30/75/150, mean 47.3), and the interaction term. ASSUMPTION (per your note 4): the brief's "interaction between terms" is implemented as BCG × interaction-frequency (primary), with MH_count × interaction-frequency as a sensitivity.

RESULTS (primary model):
- Odds ratio for BCG (main effect, at interaction frequency = 0): 0.883, 95% CI [0.285, 2.738], Wald p=0.830.
- Marginal OR for BCG at mean interaction frequency (47.3): 1.222, 95% CI [0.645, 2.314].
- Interaction BCG × interaction-frequency: OR 1.007 per unit frequency, 95% CI [0.987, 1.027], p=0.499 — no evidence the BCG effect is modified by interaction frequency.
- MH_count: OR 1.194 per additional prior condition, 95% CI [0.908, 1.570], p=0.206 (coef 0.177, SE 0.140).
- Interaction frequency: OR 1.002 per unit, 95% CI [0.989, 1.016], p=0.715 (coef 0.0025, SE 0.007).
- Proportional-odds (Brant) test: overall chi2(8)=18.98, p=0.089 — not rejected at 0.05 (per-term p: BCG 0.105, mh_count 0.091, freq 0.655, interaction 0.215).

SENSITIVITIES (all n=148): first-AE-by-AESTDTC outcome: OR BCG main 1.208 [0.388, 3.762], marginal 1.328 [0.696, 2.535]; MH_count × freq interaction model: OR BCG main 1.214 [0.641, 2.298], marginal 1.592 [0.781, 3.246], mh×freq OR 1.006 (p=0.109); patients_seen coded 1/2/3 instead of midpoints: OR BCG main 0.757 [0.155, 3.705], marginal 1.216 [0.641, 2.307]. All variants agree: no significant BCG effect.

CONCLUSION: After controlling for prior medical-history count and patients' interaction frequency (and their interaction, under the stated BCG×frequency reading), there is no evidence that BCG vaccination changes the odds of higher COVID-19 severity: the BCG odds ratio is close to 1 (main effect 0.883; 1.222 at the mean interaction frequency), with wide, non-significant CIs, and the BCG-by-interaction-frequency interaction is null (OR 1.007, p=0.499). Limitations: sparse top severity levels (8 subjects at level 3, 6 at level 4) driving wide CIs; case-only sample (subjects with a COVID-19 AE), so the OR applies to severity among infected subjects; patients_seen is banded (midpoint coding, '>100'→150 is arbitrary); Brant test is borderline (p=0.089). Executed script: /workspace/analysis_bcg_ordinal.py (exit 0).
